# Real Firefox delivery evidence

6 October 2026: the [default direct-transport comparison](../../../../docs/verification/browser-direct-transport/README.md) preserves this complete frozen corpus while observing actual libdbus requests. Untouched v1.6.0 and native default clients match all 21 cases; three explicit reads prove the outgoing observer sees peer traffic invisible to the bus monitor. `make linux-browser-target-test` runs the existing owner on both transports. The original observations and historical scope below remain unchanged.

The immutable reference is Mluva v1.6.0 at `5202477edfe4b5d8bacfa5b2e9fd6eadd9624f7f`. An external temporary collector imports the downloaded release and compares both production modules against that commit before calling them. `text_target.py` has SHA-256 `a916b65519d33b3401ebfee910c392560b86d5e70d6131aa3e6702394fef02c7`; `delivery.py` has SHA-256 `60ce68b777eee432d5e6b06c556c8bfc5af0b7f3b3926bcf012304e66b10af46`. The frozen `firefox-target-cases.json` has SHA-256 `1f5042faac2213dded8f5d473d45547cd13ce5f22b29624941c69c0289ba0f96`. Native checks read static outputs and require no interpreter.

Twenty-one cases use real windowed Firefox 154.0/build `20260818182641`, libatspi 2.60.6, GTK 4.22.4, xclip 0.13 and xdotool 4.20260303.1 under a private Openbox window manager. Firefox's main executable has SHA-256 `7a949a94c6a1b8f28e32a0e85e400ff156b2a2a2a42f7bcc5b80da79fd000a01`; the extracted xclip/xdotool/Openbox executables have SHA-256 `1a757a1ae88441c9fc6101c0750d86a1afb5cb7b2073a0ed98967c41dc292d20`, `e5c6b55bb4a9677b7d6639403e0e7e279c95b0522b792f264c32359213c20626` and `52be37f4270672e1b604a11439e06350347f1b490807da109d232cc0323ee6ac`. Distro packages were extracted only into ignored task scratch; no host packages or desktop configuration were changed.

A separate native development peer starts Firefox with an empty guarded profile and uses its real [Marionette protocol](https://firefox-source-docs.mozilla.org/remote/marionette/Protocol.html) to prepare synthetic inputs and read the DOM. The static local HTML target has SHA-256 `2baeb38dadad470eb55df1933ecb83bdcb915afb40ec5b4ebf0d344ebc8a5929`. It exposes a textarea, single-line input, distinct second input, password input, contenteditable field and button. Its own listeners independently report paste/beforeinput/input events. The peer does not supply a captured accessibility node, restoration decision, insertion acknowledgement or delivery receipt. Both clients discover real nodes, resolve the actual Firefox process through `/proc`, restore their snapshot, then call production clipboard-first delivery with snapshot-bound direct/confirmation/keyboard authorization callbacks.

The first case starts with an already-focused field before the client first initializes libatspi. The private canonical enabled-status owner is ready before Firefox starts; GTK client cache advertisement is established before its own focus can be observed. Earlier harnesses started the status owner late and produced an unrelated Firefox handler-registration warning plus clipboard-only cold capture. Correct startup removes that warning and both final clients capture/paste into the cold target. A real window manager supplies the active-window contract, and the native peer/test independently identify its process and Firefox's window/process/profile. This harness correction is not a change to the released or native production clients.

Ten cases return confirmed paste receipts, three return dispatched-but-unconfirmed receipts, seven retain clipboard-only recovery and one rejects an oversized Command selection before delivery. Observations retain exact original/final strings, UTF-16 selection/caret offsets, all five fields, final focus, event order, clipboard bytes, receipt guidance and durable history outcome. Reversed/moved/cleared/changed selections restore the captured range. Focus changing to another field or the client's own real GTK window refuses restoration; closing the tracker also refuses its retained keyboard snapshot. A further focus change between initial restore and final authorization prevents any paste event and preserves the complete clipboard text. Automatic-paste-disabled, nontext and password cases produce no paste. A read-only field and a target which prevents its paste event remain honestly unconfirmed; neither is retried. Embedded NUL remains intact in xclip while Firefox inserts only its prefix, also yielding one unconfirmed attempt. The single-line field normalizes the newline without changing its UTF-16 caret length. A contenteditable field receives one actual browser paste.

Firefox is routed through clipboard/key delivery because its accessibility editing interface can acknowledge without mutating. No input helper is faked: production delivery invokes the real X11-scoped xclip and xdotool binaries. The DOM proves insertion and one-attempt behavior independently of AT-SPI confirmation. Emoji, ZWJ and combining text exercise Gecko's UTF-16 caret contract. Selected text retains Firefox's actual padding bytes for those offsets; the exact Command limit case contains 1,000 emoji occupying 2,000 reported units, while 1,001 emoji exceeds the released limit. These are recorded dependency behaviors, not a claim that Gecko reports the same character units as GTK.

Twenty-one readiness-gated private bus monitors observe exactly three `Text.GetText` calls at `(7,17)`, `(0,2000)` and `(0,2002)`. Every delivery capture/restoration/confirmation and every password/stale/refused-paste case produces zero text reads. Command selections act as independent positive controls, so a blind monitor cannot pass as privacy proof. GTK's bridge normally offers direct application connections; the initial exploratory paired run matched browser edits but its bus-only monitors could not see those calls. The final comparisons use GNOME's supported `ATSPI_DISABLE_P2P=1` [debug connection control](https://github.com/GNOME/at-spi2-core/commit/bdf83c442845902d68f29d782d97ee32101c2b49), also verified in the distribution's [2.60.6 bridge](https://github.com/GNOME/at-spi2-core/blob/2.60.6/atk-adaptor/bridge.c). Privacy observations are explicitly scoped to the monitored message-bus transport; default direct connections after the corrected cold startup remain a separate acceptance boundary.

`dev/run-isolated-browser.sh` clears inherited credentials and creates separate network/PID namespaces, a minimal device tree and an empty `/tmp`. The virtual display, both buses, accessibility registry, window manager, home/profile and Xauthority are private. Session-service auto-activation is hidden; native assertions confirm that no portal owns its name. Loopback Marionette remains inside the private network namespace, which the peer and client independently compare with the host namespace. No microphone/audio/input/GPU device node is available, no host clipboard/input is used, and no real provider or user content is loaded. Firefox retains offline Nimbus/backup startup diagnostics unrelated to the target; final registry/client logs have no cache/registration failures. Software-only Mesa EGL avoids the separately diagnosed Xvfb/NVIDIA abort when the device tree is hidden. Only exact owned processes/groups are signaled. The final native test waits for successful peer exit and verifies disappearance of Firefox's main PID and the status owner; leaving the private PID namespace contains all descendants.

The primary owner is `actual_browser_clipboard_edits_and_focus_guards_match_the_released_client` in `browser_target.rs`, explicitly executed with `--ignored`. A regression which enables Firefox's acknowledgement-only direct editing would remove the independently observed paste/edit; counting Unicode scalars for its caret would misreport successful emoji insertion; stale authorization or a retry would mutate the second field or duplicate an observed paste event. Existing GTK and synthetic-helper tests cannot reach these real-browser/clipboard boundaries. The new checks reuse the GTK peer/monitor client support rather than duplicating it and introduce no test-only production export or injection hook. This compares the production target/delivery composition with the released composition; complete recording, preview, retry and History controllers are still unassembled.

Final source evidence is retained privately in `tmp/released-firefox-target-startup.log` and its session directory; final native evidence is in `tmp/native-firefox-target-accepted.log` and its session directory, including all monitor logs and `native-firefox-target-observations.json`. Chromium, editor and terminal insertion, default direct-connection acceptance, Wayland focus/clipboard/global keys, malformed/ambiguous trees, discovery races, complete application assembly, packaging and whole-app performance remain required. All complete-workflow rows remain Pending, the installed app/widget remain v1.6.0 and the full Rust goal stays active. The browser peer and HTML are unshipped support.
